title: A self-compliant selector-free memory with functional bismuth ferrite
authors: Suman Roy, Subhabrata Das, Priyanka Sahu, Majid Ahmadi, Sameer Kumar Mallik, Kaushik Ghosh, Saroj Prasad Dash, Satyaprakash Sahoo
abstract: In-memory computing requires selector-free operation, low variability, and stable multilevel switching, all of which remain challenging to achieve in a single system. Here, we demonstrate a robust selector-free memory based on a multiferroic BiFeO3 that combines self-compliance with stable bipolar switching, high yield, long endurance, and extended retention. We observe that BiFeO3 memristive crossbar arrays become self-compliant through a naturally formed TiOx interfacial layer, enabling forming-free bipolar switching without external selector devices, addressing major bottlenecks that have limited the practical deployment of resistive memories. The array delivers stable bipolar switching with a 97% device yield, endurance beyond 105 cycles, and data retention exceeding 105 s with low cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device variability. In addition, the devices exhibit 16 well-separated conductance states, enabling 4-bit multilevel operation via precise pulse-controlled programming for digit visualization in edge applications. Noise measurements reveal predominantly 1/f-type behavior with minimal random telegraph noise, indicating robust conductance stability across the programmable window. These results establish BiFeO3 as a practical materials platform for multibit, selector-free crossbar memories offering high reliability, making it well-suited for scalable computing architectures based on functional materials.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, highly reliable memory device utilizing bismuth ferrite (BiFeO3) that operates without external selectors. By leveraging a naturally formed interfacial layer, the device achieves stable, bipolar switching and supports 4-bit multilevel data storage. These results establish BiFeO3 as a practical material platform for next-generation, scalable computing architectures.
main_problem: The challenge in in-memory computing to achieve selector-free operation, low variability, and stable multilevel switching simultaneously.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that BiFeO3 can function as a robust, self-compliant, selector-free memory, enabling stable bipolar switching and 4-bit multilevel operation.
method: Experimental characterization of memristive crossbar arrays using functional bismuth ferrite.
model_or_system: The physical system is a multiferroic BiFeO3 memristive crossbar array. The key mechanism involves a naturally formed TiOx interfacial layer that imparts self-compliance, eliminating the need for external selector devices.
key_observables: Stable bipolar switching, 97% device yield, endurance > 10^5 cycles, retention > 10^5 s, 16 well-separated conductance states, and predominantly 1/f-type noise behavior.
important_parameters: Multilevel operation (4-bit), selector-free operation, and the material properties of BiFeO3.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the naturally formed TiOx layer facilitates the necessary self-compliance for reliable operation.
paper_structure: The paper presents a demonstration of the device's capabilities, focusing on achieving key metrics like yield, endurance, and multilevel switching using the functional material.
why_interesting: While the core physics is condensed matter/device physics, the focus on robust, high-density memory elements and functional materials is relevant to the hardware implementation aspects of quantum computing architectures.
